sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year, from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F203][F1][F10].
Operating margin rose 0.7pp, from 3.2% to 3.9%, so operating income compounded faster at 12.3% a year [F23][F32][F204].
The steps came in FY2021, when revenue rose 17.5% and operating income 23.4%, and in FY2022, when revenue rose 15.8% [D189][D190][D238].
The 10-K ties FY2021 growth to comparable sales up 16% and FY2022 to up 14%, both helped by new warehouses [P56][P42][D189][D238].
Product sales supplied 9.9pp of the 10.1% FY2026 revenue growth [D535][D434].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses was the fastest-growing product category at 19.9%, adding 3.7pp [D600][D601].
Food and Sundries added 2.6pp and Non-Foods 2.2pp, while membership fees added only 0.2pp [D560][D576][D665].
The filing excerpts provided do not explain the ancillary sales gain, so its driver remains unconfirmed [D600].
Operating income grew 12.5% on 10.1% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 4.7%, down from 9.6% in FY2024 [D435][D434][D457][D359].
Operating margin of 3.9% in FY2026 sits above its 3.4% window median and at the window high [F32][D692][D691].
Against six retail peers that is the 17th percentile, versus a 5.0% peer median [D709][D710].
Management said SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, while Canadian and Other International costs rose [P9][D460].
FY2024 operating margin rose 0.3pp on a 0.4pp cost-of-revenue effect [D349][D361], helped by ancillary gains and the absence of 2023 charter-shipping charges [P24].
The effective tax rate fell from 32.8% in FY2017 to 24.7% in FY2026, alongside net margin rising from 2.1% to 3.0% [D8][D420][F43][F52].
FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income; free cash flow of $9.38 billion was 1.02x, against a 0.99x median [F82][D421][F102][D422][D701].
Capex grew 17.0% against 10.1% revenue growth, lifting capex to 2.41x D&A from 1.71x in FY2020 [D441][D434][D423][D129].
Operating cash flow grew 18.6%, which the 10-K attributes to higher operating income and lower net inventory investment [P6][D439].
FY2022 free cash flow fell to 0.60x net income, the window low, as operating cash flow dropped 17.5%; the excerpts give no cause [D226][D699][D243].
Net cash was $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, on $21.3 billion of cash and investments against $6.16 billion of debt [D427][D428][D425][D426].
That ranks at the 100th percentile of six retail peers, against a peer median net cash of -4.4% of revenue [D715][D716].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $3.31 billion, 35.2% of free cash flow, and diluted shares ended 0.8% above FY2017 [D429][D430][X100][X91].
Long-term debt fell to $3.91 billion from $5.71 billion, with the 10-K citing debt repayments among financing outflows [F192][F191][P4].
FY2022 cash conversion is the main flag: free cash flow was 0.60x net income, the window low, and the excerpts do not state the cause [D226][D699].
Capex grew 17.0% against 10.1% revenue growth in FY2026, and the 10-K describes investing as primarily capital expenditure [D441][D434][P5].
FY2026 gross margin includes a gain from IEEPA tariff refunds, which management plans to largely reinvest in member prices, so that gain is partly passed on [P12][P15].
Margin headroom is thin, with operating margin at the 17th percentile of peers [D709][F32].
An operating margin above the 3.9% FY2026 high would confirm the trend; a fall below the 3.4% window median would reverse it, visible in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D691][D692].
Free cash flow to net income at or above the 0.99x median would confirm conversion; a reading near the 0.60x low would repeat FY2022, visible in the FY2027 10-K [D701][D699].
Capex growth should converge toward revenue growth of 10.1%; growth still near 17.0% with free cash flow margin below the 2.8% median would reverse the cash story [D434][D441][D698].
